mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is a baseline effect that holds in normal monetary conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals an imminent monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) signals a robust labor market, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: During the post-pandemic housing recovery regime (HOUST > 1000 and RSAFS > 400000), the housing market's rebound signals strong consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1000 and RSAFS > 400000, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) rises above 105, it signals strong economic activity and corporate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 105, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index (CPIAUCSL) below 240 (indicating inflation below 2.5% from the 1982-1984 base) signals stable price conditions, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL < 240, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.25% and the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) is below 240, it signals a dovish monetary policy environment that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS < 0.25% and CPIAUCSL < 240, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% YoY), the economy is growing strongly, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% YoY, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).
